content.body:
Living with a ferritin of 8 is like trying to breathe at 14,000 feet. Every single day. Except you're standing at sea level and nobody believes you.

That photo is me standing on top of a 14,000-foot mountain. Thumbs up. Tears streaming behind my goggles.

A year ago I couldn't walk to my car without stopping to catch my breath.

Here's what changed.

At 43, I had to choose between pretending I was fine or admitting that my body was shutting down and nobody could tell me why.

I couldn't do both.

The exhaustion was so bad that every single day I'd spend my mornings:

Gripping the stair railing at work so hard my knuckles turned white because my legs felt like they'd buckle

Sitting in my car during lunch with the seat reclined because I physically could not make it to the break room and back

Pulling clumps of hair off my pillow before my husband woke up so he wouldn't see how bad it was getting

My hairstylist stopped pretending. She put her hands on my shoulders and said: "Hon, you need to see someone about this. This isn't normal."

My doctor looked at my labs for three seconds and said: "Your iron is normal. Maybe try biotin."

My husband stopped suggesting weekend hikes — something we used to do every month — because he knew what my face would look like when he asked.

The face that said: "I want to, but my body won't let me."

My breaking point came at my daughter's field day at school.

Parents were invited to run the three-legged race with their kids.

My daughter grabbed my hand. "Mom, we're gonna win!"

I made it maybe 40 feet.

I had to stop. Bent over. Hands on my knees. Gasping.

Other parents jogged past us. Some of them looked back.

My daughter's face went from excited to confused to embarrassed.

"Mom? Are you okay?"

I lied and said yes.

But I wasn't fine.

I was 43 years old, standing in a field on a perfect Saturday morning, and I couldn't run 40 feet with my daughter without almost passing out.

I watched the other moms laughing, crossing the finish line, picking up their kids.

I couldn't even make it halfway.

That night, after my daughter went to bed, I sat on the bathroom floor pulling another clump of hair from the drain and cried.

Not from the hair loss.

From the realization that this thing — whatever it was — had stolen my ability to be the mom I wanted to be.

My energy. My hair. My weekends with my husband. My confidence. My daughter's face when I couldn't keep up with her.

I looked at my husband sleeping in our bed and thought: "Poor guy has probably given up on having the woman he married back."

The next morning, I made an appointment with my fourth doctor.

Dr. Nguyen. A dermatologist.

My friend Carla from work had insisted: "She's different. She actually listens."

I'd heard that before. But I was desperate.

When Dr. Nguyen walked into the exam room, she didn't open her computer.

She pulled up a chair. Sat down. And said: "Tell me everything."

So I did.

I told her about the three years of getting worse with no explanation. The hair loss accelerating every month. The exhaustion so severe I'd fall asleep in my car during lunch. The three doctors who said "your iron is normal." The $500 I'd spent on biotin and collagen that did nothing. The brain fog so bad I'd forget words mid-sentence. The look on my daughter's face at field day.

When I finished, I expected her to sigh and reach for a prescription pad.

Instead, she picked up a marker.

She drew three connected arrows on the exam table paper.

"Your body isn't broken," she said. "It's starving."

"And that's why nothing you've tried has worked."

"Every doctor you've seen checked your hemoglobin — your circulating iron. And it looked fine."

"But none of them checked your ferritin — your iron STORAGE."

"Imagine your body is a house. Hemoglobin is the electricity running through the wires right now. Ferritin is the generator in the basement."

"Your lights are flickering, and every electrician you've called has said 'the wires look fine.' But nobody's gone to the basement to check if the generator is empty."

She explained that when ferritin drops, three systems collapse simultaneously.

Your hair follicles starve first — they need ferritin above 70 to function properly. Below that, they enter a starvation cycle. The growth phase shortens. The shedding accelerates. You're not losing hair because of stress or genetics. You're losing it because your follicles are starving.

Your mitochondria can't produce energy efficiently. That's why you feel like you're trying to breathe at altitude while standing at sea level. That's the gasping on the stairs. The brain fog. The falling asleep at lunch. Your body is running on empty.

And the standard treatment — ferrous sulfate — only absorbs at about 10 to 15 percent. The rest sits in your gut causing nausea and constipation. Even what absorbs can't convert into stored ferritin without the right cofactors.

"So you take iron for months. Your hemoglobin stays normal. Your doctor says you're fine."

"But your ferritin never moves. And your hair keeps falling out."

For the first time in three years, someone was explaining WHY my body was failing me.

Not just saying "your iron looks fine." Actually explaining the mechanism.

"So what do I do?" I asked.

"I could send you for iron infusions. They'll spike your ferritin fast. But at $800 to $1,600 per session, and without the cofactors to maintain your stores, most women crash back down within weeks."

"I could prescribe higher-dose ferrous sulfate. But you'll be nauseous, constipated, and your ferritin probably still won't move."

"The women who raise their ferritin and keep it up do something different."

"They fix all three systems at once: the absorption, the conversion, AND the storage."

She wrote on her prescription pad:

Iron bisglycinate (NOT ferrous sulfate — absorbs up to 4x better)

Vitamin C (for enhanced absorption)

Vitamin B6 + B12 + Methylfolate (for the conversion pathway into stored ferritin)

"Find something with ALL of these. Together. Not separately."

I went home and started searching.

Most supplements had iron. Maybe vitamin C.

Nothing had the complete conversion pathway.

Then I found a thread in a Facebook group for women with low ferritin.

The kind of group where women post their lab results at 2am and tell the truth about how desperate they are.

Dozens of comments. All about the same thing: FerraVital.

"Ferritin stuck at 9 for over a year. Hit 72 in ten weeks on this."

"I can actually get through a day without feeling like I'm dying. For the first time in years."

"The shedding stopped. I have baby hairs. I'm not even exaggerating. Baby hairs."

I checked the ingredients against Dr. Nguyen's list. It was all there. Every single thing she told me to find. In one capsule.

I'd already spent over $1,400 on ferrous sulfate, biotin, collagen, Floradix, doctor appointments where they told me I was "fine." Three years. Zero answers.

$35 for something that could actually fix the root cause? What did I have to lose besides another clump of hair?

I ordered it.

Day 3: No stomach pain. For the first time ever with iron.

Day 7: I woke up and didn't hit snooze. Not wired. Not caffeinated. Just... not exhausted. For the first time in years.

Day 14: Less hair in the shower drain. Noticeably less. I kept checking. I wasn't imagining it.

Day 21: The brain fog lifted. I followed an entire meeting without drifting.

Day 30: My husband said "You seem like yourself again." I didn't know what to say. Because he was right.

Day 45: My daughter asked me to go on a bike ride. I said yes. And I meant it. We rode for an hour. Something I couldn't do two months ago.

Three months later, I went back to Dr. Nguyen.

"Let's check your ferritin," she said.

I held my breath.

"74."

I burst into tears.

It had been stuck at 8 for three years. Through ferrous sulfate. Through Floradix. Through everything.

74.

She examined my scalp. "New growth along your hairline and your part. Your follicles are being fed again."

Six months later, I climbed a mountain.

Not a metaphor. An actual mountain. Over 14,000 feet.

I stood at the summit crying behind my goggles.

Because a year ago, I couldn't walk up one flight of stairs.

And now I was standing on top of a mountain.

I can run with my daughter without stopping.

I can hike with my husband on weekends again.

I can sit through meetings without my brain shutting off.

I got my life back. Not just my energy. Not just my hair. My entire life.

Here's what makes me furious.

Low ferritin affects tens of millions of women.

The lab range starts at 10 and doctors call 12 "normal."

But your hair needs 70+. Your mitochondria need 70+. Your brain needs 70+.

Millions of women are walking around feeling like they're suffocating at sea level and being told they're "fine."

The exhaustion isn't the problem. The hair loss isn't the problem. They're symptoms.

Fix the absorption, the conversion, and the storage — and the symptoms stop.

FerraVital has all of it. The exact nutrients your body needs to rebuild ferritin, feed your follicles, and fuel your cells.

👉 Try FerraVital Risk-Free for 90 Days

P.S. A year ago, I was pretending to check my phone at the bottom of a staircase so nobody would see me gasping for air.

Last month, I stood on top of a mountain.

Ferritin 8 → 74. One capsule before bed.

You don't have to keep living at altitude when you're standing at sea level.
